claim: When two memory records assert different values for the same key, both are retained and the conflict is surfaced — the newer one never silently overwrites the older, and the key has no answer until someone resolves it.

steps.label: run-1 writes a key nobody has claimed
run-2 asserts the same value from a different source
run-3 asserts a different value for the same key
steps.evidence: quarantine holds 1 conflict; both sources still attributable
steps.note: Under last-write-wins the drift becomes the memory and the record it replaced is gone. A model that drifts writes its drift last.

steps.label: reading a key that is under conflict
steps.note: Returning either side would be the silent choice the store exists to prevent. Returning the older one is last-write-wins with extra steps.

steps.label: resolving the conflict to a value nobody asserted
steps.note: Resolution is a decision between what was asserted.
